info.title: Posiverse OpenAPI
info.description:
# Introduction
This is the OpenAPI service for the Posiverse device management platform.  You can 
- manage your Devices, Groups, Settings, Firmwares, Products, Tenants, Users
- create Tags and associate them with your Devices, Groups or Users.  
- view all the logs associated with your Devices and Users for auditing purpose.
Posiverse is provided by Positioning Universal Inc.  You can find out more information about Positiong Universal at the [website](https://www.positioninguniversal.com)

# Pagination
Results that can result in an array of objects being returned can cause in the result to be paginated.  The 4 related headers are:
- x-total-count: The total number of objects to be returned.  Always returned.
- x-page-count: The number of objects returned in current response.  Always returned. If this value equals x-total-count then full result set is contained in response.
- x-page-start: The offset into the total count of objects the current response starts at (0 based),  Always returned.
- x-next-page-url: The partial URL of the next page, you need to prepend the server URL used to create original request.  If this header is not present then no more pages exist.

Unauthorized.description: API key is missing or unauthorized

Throttled.description: Too many requests in last minute

BadRequest.description: Request contains incorrect or unparseable data

Forbidden.description: The authenticated user is forbidden from attempting this operation

bearerAuth.description: Posiverse currently offers one form of authentication which is a bearer API Key authorization: * You must obtain an account from the Posiverse Team in order to get a useful API Key. * Header must be added to each request * Separate API Key must be used for Test backend and Production backend. * API Keys can be accessed through the Posiverse UI by clicking on User Profile. * API Keys can be changed at any time in the UI.
bearerAuth.name: posiverse-auth-key

tags.name: Commands
tags.description: Add commands to queue for device.  If device is connected then it will receive all queued commands.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: Read all devices. Read device properties, scratchpad, and settings synched.  Modify device name, description and move it to another group.

tags.name: Groups
tags.description: Read all groups.  Changing group names and description.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Read settings for a device or group. Change settings on a device or a group.  When a group's settings are changed then all new devices moved to group will get default group settings.  Existing devices in group will not be affected by change in group's settings.

tags.name: Logs
tags.description: View log data for device activity, user activity, and telemetry activity if it is available (only in special cases)

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: Read all tags.  Create new tags. Modify existing tags with new name.  Delete existing tags (if no associated TagMaps).  Tags are used to organize data and can be associated with Devices/Groups/Users.

tags.name: TagMaps
tags.description: Create new tag map.  Modify value associated with existing tag map.  Delete existing tag map.  Tag maps associate a tag with one of Device/Group/User and a unique value.

tags.name: Tenants
tags.description: Read all tenants. Modify tenant name and description.  The ability to read multiple tenants is only meaningful for customers who have access to multiple tenants.

tags.name: VirtualConsole
tags.description: Virtual Console actions.  This is a feature which allows connecting to a device over the Internet as if connecting through the serial port.  You simply use this API to write commands to device and poll the read queue for responses.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Read all users.  Modify user's name and description.
